newsitem.title: USA: Recording industry agrees on DVD format - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Recording industry agrees on DVD format - NYT.

text.p: Leading record companies and consumer electronics manufacturers have agreed on the broad technical guidelines for DVD audio format, which the recording industry has decided to introduce as a replacement for compact disks, The New York Times said in Monday's editions.
The paper said the accord signals a fundamental shift in the recorded music business, away from two-channel stereo sound to multi-channel audio, using six speakers.

The new disks and players, most likely to reach the market in about two years at prices initially higher than current compact disks and CD players, may tempt consumers to update their sound systems, the article said.
The new disks will be able to store seven times more digital data than today's CDs, the paper said.
